children: Moneyview Limited, one of India’s largest digital lending platforms, has fixed its initial public offering price band at ₹32 to ₹34 per equity share, with the issue opening for public subscription on September 24, 2026, and closing on September 28, 2026. Anchor investor bidding is scheduled for September 23.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue aggregating up to ₹750 crore and an offer for sale of up to 100,494,200 equity shares by existing shareholders, including co-founders Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal. Bids can be made for a minimum lot of 441 equity shares. The shares will be listed on both BSE and NSE. Axis Capital, BofA Securities India, IIFL Capital Services, and Kotak Mahindra Capital are the book running lead managers.

The company manages a personal loan portfolio of approximately ₹22,520 crore across six million borrowers and counts 140 million registered users on its platform, roughly 10 per cent of India’s working-age population. About 80 per cent of its customers are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, with an average monthly income of ₹45,000.

Moneyview operates a capital-light model, with approximately 75 per cent of its loan book funded through lending partners under a Loan Service Provider arrangement, keeping its own balance sheet exposure at around 25 per cent. The company reported a profit after tax of close to ₹400 crore in the last financial year, with ₹174 crore posted in the first quarter of FY27 alone. Revenue has been growing at 40-45 per cent year-on-year, while profits have expanded at over 65 per cent.
The company originally sought ₹1,500 crore in fresh capital but revised the amount downward.we do not need 1,500 crore. 750 crore is sufficient for us to stay on track.”

Of the fresh issue proceeds, ₹325 crore is earmarked for deployment under Default Loss Guarantee arrangements to grow the off-balance sheet lending business, with a portion also directed toward strengthening the NBFC’s capital base.
The company processes approximately two lakh loan applications daily, using over one lakh data variables per borrower for credit underwriting, with minimal human intervention in the process.

title: Moneyview sets IPO price band at ₹32-34, eyes ₹750 cr fresh capital
